step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture describes Haptik's analytics ingestion platform for conversational AI chatbots, handling both real-time metrics and long-term archival. Real-time chat metadata from Mobile, Web, and Messaging Platforms streams into Kinesis. The real-time branch pulls data from Kinesis into Logstash on EC2, indexes it into Elasticsearch (OpenSearch), and serves an in-house custom dashboard for clients and internal monitoring. The archival branch triggers a Lambda function from Kinesis to store batch data in S3, where AWS Glue catalogs the schema and Amazon Athena queries historical dataset metrics.

graph.name: Haptik Conversational AI Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Haptik processes over 40-50 million chat and voice messages monthly across channels (Web, Mobile, WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter). Metadata streams into Kinesis and splits into real-time analytics (Logstash, Elasticsearch, Custom Dashboard) and historical batch archival (Lambda, S3, Glue, Athena).

edges.notes: Mobile client sends conversation metadata to Kinesis stream.
Web client sends conversation metadata to Kinesis stream.
Messaging platform channels send conversation metadata to Kinesis stream.
Logstash pulls real-time conversation data stream from Kinesis.
Logstash transforms and indexes data into Elasticsearch.
Custom dashboard queries real-time metrics and conversation trends from Elasticsearch.
Kinesis triggers Lambda function upon event arrival for historical pipeline processing.
Lambda processes batch data and stores it long term in S3 bucket.
AWS Glue crawls S3 storage to define catalog schema.
Glue catalog provides schema definition to Amazon Athena for querying S3.
